usageGuidance: Use these three excerpts as examples of representational choices. Their project-specific names and facts are not evidence for the new task. Choose the hierarchy, depth, branching, density, and relationship types that fit the supplied source; do not reproduce the examples' exact shape, category names, counts, or sequence. Not every diagram needs every relationship type. The [M]/[O]/[C]/[D] notation belongs to these examples and is not mandatory unless the task explicitly requests it. These are output-style excerpts, not paired source-to-diagram demonstrations. All come from one architecture diagram, so they provide structural and semantic variety within that diagram, not domain or notation diversity.

examples.ascii:
[O] CanvasWorkspace manages open documents
|-- [M] Exposes document lifecycle and persistence notifications
|-- [O] Creates, subscribes to and disposes CanvasSessions
|   `-- drafts[documentId]: CanvasDraft
|       |-- Document identity and save baseline
|       |   |-- representationId / name / revisionId
|       |   `-- savedName / savedScene / savedEdges
|       |-- Workspace presentation
|       |   `-- busy / hidden / viewport / focusBox
|       `-- session: CanvasSession
|           |-- [O] Retains MappingDocumentController
|           |-- [M] Exposes coordinated session stores
|           |   |-- document
|           |   |-- presentation / selection
|           |   `-- controls / geometry / status
|           `-- [C] onCommit()
|               `-- notify workspace persistence
`-- controllers[documentId]
    `-- [D] indexes the controllers retained by sessions
examples.selectionRationale: An asymmetric ownership hierarchy: lifecycle operations, nested retained state, a callback, and an index referring back to owned objects.
examples.overfittingGuidance: Learn selective expansion and explicit responsibility. Do not infer that every owner needs drafts, sessions, controllers, or a callback.

nodes(): DisplayNode[]
|-- [D] document + presentation + geometry -> public registry
|   `-- derived nodes; not a second authoritative document
|-- Common identity and hierarchy
|   `-- id / read-time version / childIds / expansion
|-- Grid nodes
|   |-- diagram or group; authoritative boxId
|   |-- [D] GridBox layout -> cell bounds

|   `-- diagram instance -> DiagramContent

examples.selectionRationale: A result-oriented read model: inputs produce a public registry, common properties precede contrasting node families, and only one family expands into concrete variants.
examples.overfittingGuidance: Learn common-versus-specific grouping and inputs-to-result relationships. Do not reproduce the grid/floating split, variant count, coordinate system, or this depth unless supported.

examples.title: Agent request flow
examples.normalization: Remove the first 4 ancestor/branch columns from each line; retain all labels and relative descendant indentation.
examples.rawAscii:
|-- [M] Agent access adapts external requests to document operations
|   `-- [C] MCP -> HTTP backend -> AgentDiagrammingSessionService.exec
|       |-- synchronous canvas / nodes / edges API
|       `-- Live document request
|           `-- [C] CanvasSessionBridge -> useAgentCanvasBridge
|               `-- attached session's MappingDocumentController
|                   |-- reads -> exposed read models
|                   `-- edits -> applyUpdate(expectedVersion, operations)
examples.ascii:
[M] Agent access adapts external requests to document operations
`-- [C] MCP -> HTTP backend -> AgentDiagrammingSessionService.exec
    |-- synchronous canvas / nodes / edges API
    `-- Live document request
        `-- [C] CanvasSessionBridge -> useAgentCanvasBridge
            `-- attached session's MappingDocumentController
                |-- reads -> exposed read models
                `-- edits -> applyUpdate(expectedVersion, operations)
examples.selectionRationale: A short dynamic path across boundaries, ending in a read/edit fork; intermediate hops are compressed inline.
examples.overfittingGuidance: Learn concise call flow and selective branching. Do not infer that every process has MCP, HTTP, a bridge, or a binary read/edit fork.
